messages.body_plain:
I am encountering the error:

No valid local directories in property: mapred.local.dir

Whenever rhex tries to read and return data to the console.  Instead I
see: Error in doCMD(rhoptions()$cmd["s2b"], infiles = files, ofile =
tf1, ilocal = dolocal, ... which is caused an "invalid"
mapred.local.dir.

However when I look in my mapred-site.xml file on the master I have:

<property>
  <name>mapred.local.dir</name>
  <value>/mnt/hadoop/mapred/local</value>
  <final>true</final>
</property>

Which seems normal.  Any suggestions?

I am trying to run Rhipe 0.57 on EC2 (Fedora 32 bit ami-6159bf08).

is most probably(i think) because you started your cluster with less
than 2 nodes.
e.g.
python hadoop-ec2 launch-cluster --env REPO=testing   --env
HADOOP_VERSION=0.20 test2 5

the last number must be greater than 2 ( i think 2 will work, but 1
wont!)

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.body_plain:
Sorry for (what turned out to be) a double post.  Thank you for your
quick response.

Unfortunately I had the same problem running a cluster of > 2 as
well.  I tried running 4 slaves the first time actually.

There seems to be a permissions issue with the /mnt/hadoop/mapred/
local folder for the root user.  I added chmod a+rwxt /mnt*/hadoop/
mapred/local to the hadoop-ec2-init-remote.sh file at the end of
configure_hadoop() and that now everything seems to work.

I diff'ed the .sh script provided by Cloudera with yours and the only
difference was installing R/Rhipe so I'm curious why I had permissions
issues, perhaps something else is going on?

messages.subject: [rhipe] rhsave/rhload Using Shared Files
messages.body_plain:
Hello again.

I was wondering if anyone had experience using shared files with
Rhipe.  It seems the example in the documentation 6.1.2 Using Shared
Files and Side Effects is not fully fleshed out.  However the main
issue I believe I am encountering is with rhsave and rhload, one of
which does not seem to be functioning properly.

For example:

> p = matrix(rnorm(3000),60,50)
> ls()
[1] "p"
> rhsave(p,file="/tmp/p.Rdata")
> rm(p)
> ls()
character(0)
> rhload(file="/tmp/p.Rdata")
> p
Error: object "p" not found

I'm not sure what is going on, perhaps I am using the functions
incorrectly but this is also preventing me from using shared files
following the example.

Also, regarding the documentation:

h=rhlapply(length(simlist) ,func=function(r){
@#@# do something from data loaded from session.Rdata
pdf("tmp/a.pdf") plot(animage) dev.off()},
17
rhipe Documentation, Release 0.59
setup=expression({ load("session.Rdata")
}), hadoop=list(mapred.map.tasks=1000), shared.files=("/tmp/
session.Rdata"))

I am assuming at some point before rhsave(...,file=("/tmp/
session.Rdata")) is called and that in the last line shared.files=
should just be shared= ?

Thanks for the help!

--

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] map/reduce key sorting
messages.body_plain:
When it comes to sorting you might be in trouble. Nothing is text in Rhipe -
everything from reading in data, sending to the map, from map to reduce(thus
including the shuffling and sorting) is done using binary bytes and all
comparisons are are byte sequence comparisons

So text e.g "field1 field2" is written out as

08 00 2a 0f 0a 0d 66 69 65 6c 64 31 20 66 69 65 6c 64 32

and indeed these might preserve lexicographic sorting(assuming string lengths
are not varint encoded) - but I've never checked for this.

So your keys are numbers? Numbers ought to sort, but I don't know (and doubt)
that numerical order will be preserved when the byte representations(protocol
buffer) are compared.

> mapred=list(mapred.text.key.partitioner.options="-k1n")

Will probably not work since there is never any text writable used (except for
reading in text files, but not between map and reduce)

Adding in custom partitioners (e.g. partition on the first element of an atomic string vector) though possible, would probably slow things down a lot. Still it is a good idea to have as an option.

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: map/reduce key sorting
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
Apologies for the long delay, I've been trying to fix some papers.

>After comparing many serialized numbers and char strings, serializing
>does indeed preserve lexicographic ordering.

Still surprising.

>However I am noticing that sorting is not occurring at all, contrary
>to what I stated earlier.  I believe I was testing on too small of a
>sample before and it just happened to have sorted them correctly. It
>seems that at some level Hadoop must do some sorting to collect k/v
>pairs with the same keys but I am not too sure what is going on and
>how to force a complete sorting of the keys.

If you look at the raw bytes the keys for a give part** file will be sorted -
the sorting happens on the byte level. If you notice value sorting (as in your
first paragraph) this needs to be proved.

>
>Can you perhaps shed some light on how streaming is called?  The
>streaming doc indicates that there is a secondary sort option for the
>keys.
>
Streaming internals have been re-written, the entire java program uses
RHBytesWritable as key and value. Not a single mention of Double, Integer or
Text. Streaming allows the secondary sort etc because it has a different
partitioner - I have been thinking of implementing a partitioner but this can
cause many surprising side effects.

So to summarize, your keys *are* sorted (Hadoop will do this) but at the byte
level which might not be of any help at the value level.

Regards
Saptarshi
